{"slug": "website-builder-for-law-firms", "title": "AI Website Builder for Law Firms: Launch in Minutes", "metaTitle": "AI Website Builder for Law Firms: Launch in Minutes | Kodely", "metaDescription": "Describe your law firm in plain English and Kodely builds a real, professional site with practice areas, attorney bios, and a contact form — live in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for law firms", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

A law firm website has one job: convince a stressed, skeptical visitor that this firm can be trusted with their case, and make it easy for them to reach out. That means most law firm sites fail for the same reasons — they bury the practice areas, hide the attorneys behind stock photography, and make contact harder than it needs to be. Kodely builds the site that avoids all three, from a plain-English description, in one sitting.

What law firm websites actually need

Before you write a single prompt, it helps to know what a visitor is actually looking for. Almost every law firm site needs to answer four questions fast:

  • What do you handle? A clear list of practice areas — family law, personal injury, estate planning, criminal defense, whatever the firm actually does — stated up front, not buried in a PDF.
  • Who will represent me? Attorney bios with real credentials: bar admissions, years practicing, notable experience, education.
  • Can I trust you? Credibility signals — client testimonials, case results summaries, awards, affiliations, years in business.
  • How do I reach you? A visible phone number, office address, and a contact form that takes two seconds to find, on every page.

Get those four right and the site is doing its job. Everything else — blog posts, FAQs, a resources page — is secondary.

Must-have sections for a law firm site

In practice, that translates into a fairly standard page structure:

  • Homepage — firm name, tagline, primary practice areas, a strong call to action, and a snapshot of why the firm is credible.
  • Practice Areas — one section or page per area of law, written for a worried potential client, not another lawyer.
  • Attorney Bios — a dedicated page or section per attorney, or per named partner, with headshots and credentials.
  • About / Firm Overview — the firm's history, values, and what makes it different from the firm down the street.
  • Testimonials or Results — short client quotes or general outcome summaries that build confidence without overpromising.
  • Contact — phone, address, office hours, and a simple form so a visitor can request a consultation without picking up the phone.

A real prompt for a law firm site

You do not need a spec document. You need one clear paragraph. Here is an example prompt that works well in Kodely for a general-practice firm:

“Build a website for Harlan & Cole Law, a family and personal injury law firm in Denver, Colorado. Homepage should have a strong headline, a short list of our three practice areas (family law, personal injury, estate planning), and a call to action to request a consultation. Include a dedicated Practice Areas page with a short section for each area. Add an Attorneys page with bios for two partners, Maria Cole and David Harlan, including their bar admissions and years of experience. Include an About page covering the firm's history and values, and a Contact page with our office address, phone number, and a consultation request form. Use a navy and gold color scheme that feels serious and trustworthy, not flashy.”

That single prompt gives Kodely everything it needs: the practice areas, the people, the tone, and the pages.

What Kodely generates from that prompt

Kodely does not return a mockup or a page of static HTML. It generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application — actual component files you could hand to a developer. Every project starts from a hand-built foundation codebase, so the Practice Areas cards, the attorney bio layout, and the navigation are built from real, reusable UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav) rather than one-off HTML blocks. As Kodely builds, you watch a live preview render the actual compiled app, not a static image of what it might look like.

One honest limitation worth stating plainly: Kodely builds the site — the practice area pages, the bios, the credibility content, and a consultation request form on the front end. It does not generate a backend, a database, online payments, or a real appointment-booking system. If your firm needs actual scheduling or client intake automation behind the scenes, that's a separate system you'd connect later. What you get from Kodely is a professional, credible marketing and information site, with a contact form UI ready for a lead to fill out.

Customizing your site

Once the first version exists, refine it the same way you built it: describe the change in chat. “Make the Attorneys page a two-column grid” or “Add a fourth practice area for estate planning” both work, and Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes rather than regenerating the whole site. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change goes in a direction you don't like, rolling back to the previous version is free and instant. You can also open the code view at any point to see and copy the actual generated source files.

Publishing live

When the site is ready, publishing is one click. Kodely puts it live on a real public URL at yourfirmname.kodely.site — included free, with no separate hosting step or cost, and every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live. There's no custom domain support yet, so the site lives at your kodely.site subdomain, which is often enough for testing a new firm site or standing up a placeholder while a full domain migration is planned.

FAQ

Does Kodely build a real booking or client intake system for my firm?

No. Kodely builds the front-end site — practice areas, attorney bios, and a consultation request form UI. It does not generate a working backend, database, or scheduling system behind that form.

Can I use my own domain, like harlanandcolelaw.com?

Not yet. Every site published from Kodely today lives at a free yourname.kodely.site subdomain.

Can I download the code and host it myself?

Not currently. You can view and copy the generated source files from inside Kodely, but there is no full-project export or zip download yet.

What does it cost to build a law firm site?

New accounts get 750 free credits with no credit card required, which is enough to build and iterate on a site like the one above. If you need more, top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, and credits never expire. A build that fails to compile is never charged.

Is this only for solo attorneys, or can a multi-partner firm use it too?

Both. The example above uses two partners, but you can describe as many attorneys, practice areas, and office locations as your firm actually has — Kodely builds the pages to match.

Ready to see your firm's site built from a single prompt? Build your law firm site free and publish it today.
